rv.q: Once more, there is abundant use of the theatre’s backstage and outside spaces and what seemed exciting for Sunset loses lustre when repeated so soon and so similarly. Our first sighting of Holland is a filmed one, in a backstage corridor: we glimpse the back of Romeo’s head, black hoodie up, cigarette smoke trailing.
Tom Holland and Francesca Amewudah-Rivers are tremulously intense lovers in Jamie Lloyd’s stark, dark take on Shakespeare’s tragedy
Most of their conversations, just like the majority throughout, are not done facing one another, but facing the audience, allowing audience members to see the full level of expression as they speak.
It turns out that, aside from some harmless frippery on the edges of the production, this is a remarkably strong Romeo + Juliet, performed in the round at Circle in the Square.

Starring Tom Holland as Romeo and Francesca Amewudah-Rivers as Juliet, this highly anticipated interpretation unfortunately falls flat. Entering the auditorium, you hear very loud electronic music that is reminiscent of the American Horror Story theme tune.
'A daring, risky balance between tradition and innovation', Arlecchino & Felicity's press material claims, that creates 'an international language' and 'new linguistic code'.

cn.t: A sleek, well-acted production with thoughtful casting choices and strong staging, but critics find it emotionally hollow where it matters most, failing to generate the heartbreak essential to Shakespeare's tragedy.
